attempts.demonstration: Start from the exact target using N for the original request. Take any valid arrangement of N new flowers. After its earlier new flowers match the algorithm, compare its next position p with the algorithm's earliest legal position g. Position p is a candidate, so g exists and g<=p. Moving only that new flower to g is compatible with original flowers and earlier choices because the code checks those neighbors. Later new flowers are farther right than p, so their spacing cannot shrink when p moves left. Preserve all N flowers and repeat. Thus a feasible N-flower arrangement implies the algorithm can place N and return true. A false return rules out such an arrangement. Include the n=0 return, valid successful placement, and finite-scan termination.
